html:
A Prussian naturalist and explorer whose journey through the Americas from 1799 to 1804 helped found modern geography and ecology. He was born in Berlin; his brother Wilhelm was a statesman and founder of the University of Berlin.

With the French botanist Aimé Bonpland, he travelled through Venezuela and up the Orinoco, then to Cuba, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru and Mexico, and finally to the United States, where he met Thomas Jefferson. He measured everything: heights, temperatures, magnetism, plants. He climbed most of the way up Chimborazo, then thought the highest mountain on earth, and drew how plants change with altitude, an idea at the root of ecology. He saw nature as one web of linked parts, and warned that clearing forests changed the climate.

Back in Europe he spent decades writing up the journey and later wrote Cosmos, a grand account of the universe. He inspired Charles Darwin, and his descriptions of Spanish America inspired Simón Bolívar. The cold Humboldt Current off Peru is one of many things named after him.
